title: Audit event schema for explicit intent and state-transition capture
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define an audit event schema and taxonomy that explicitly captures operator intent, canonical state transitions, and an efficient diff encoding suitable for RBAC v2, SSO/SAML-linked events, and admin controls. Produce storage and indexing guidance so events are searchable by actor, target, request/trace id, and by high-risk signal (privilege change, policy override, impersonation).
background_and_problem_statement: Current audit events are inconsistent in how they represent: the initiating intent (what the user intended vs what the system applied), the concrete state before/after an admin operation, and how role inheritance and SAML-linked attributes are resolved.

We need a single schema that supports: searchable metadata, compact diffs for storage efficiency, full-snapshot fallback for regulatory needs, and cryptographic integrity hints for post-facto verification.
This ticket covers schema design, encoding format decision, redaction rules, ingestion hints for Console and SIEM, and a migration strategy for existing audit consumers.
acceptance_criteria: A stable event envelope is documented with field names and example values for: event_id, timestamp, event_type, intent, actor, actor_resolution, target, target_type, pre_state_digest, post_state_digest, diff_blob, saml_context, request_id, trace_id, outcome, severity, retention_class, and signature_hint.
A recommended diff encoding is chosen with rationale and two reference implementations (encode/decode) for server-side generation and consumer-side application.
RBAC v2-specific guidance: how to log role assignment changes, policy edits, and resolved inheritance snapshots vs incremental diffs.
SAML/SSO guidance: which attributes to capture (assertion id, identity provider, attribute confidence) and how to link to actor_resolution without storing raw assertions.
Searchability: examples of indexed fields and retention_class rules for compliance vs cost-optimized tiers.
Security review completed and sign-off from SecEng and Privacy for redaction rules.
Integration plan for Console incident view and SIEM export documented with minimal consumer migration steps.
technical_details: Event envelope design: a shallow enum-backed envelope where every field is an atomic scalar (string) or a compact base64 blob. Consumers parse the envelope to reconstruct richer structures; storage avoids nested JSON for fast indexing.

Core envelope fields (strings): event_id, ts, event_type, operation, intent, request_id, trace_id, source, outcome, severity, retention_class, actor_id, actor_type, actor_resolution_hint, target_id, target_type, pre_state_digest, post_state_digest, diff_blob_b64_gzip, saml_link_id, idp_alias, signature_hint.

Intent vs operation: 'intent' captures the user/operator expressed intention (e.g., 'promote-role', 'revoke-session', 'create-service-principal'), while 'operation' is the normalized system action executed (e.g., 'role_assignment.apply'). Both are strings and are recommended to be drawn from a canonical vocabulary maintained in docs.

Diff encoding decision: selected "MOP" (Mnemonic Operational Patch) — a tiny text-based patch format optimized for common admin mutations. Rationale: smaller than full JSON snapshots, easier to diff/merge for identity/policy objects, human-readable, and friendly to line-oriented compression. Store diff_blob as gzip then base64 to ensure ASCII-safe envelopes.

MOP format primitives: add <path> <json>, remove <path>, replace <path> <json>, meta <key> <value>. Example lines: 'replace /roles/2/permissions ["read","write"]' or 'add /members/- {"id":"svc-23","type":"service"}'.

Fallback for complex edits: if MOP would exceed size threshold (configurable, default 16KB) or contains PII that cannot be redacted safely, store a sanitized full_snapshot_blob instead and mark retention_class=legal_hold_required.

Pre/Post state digests: use SHA-256 hex strings of canonical-collapsed JSON to quickly detect replay/ordering issues without storing full state. Implementation note: canonicalization step must sort object keys and normalize timestamps to RFC3339 trimmed seconds.

Actor resolution model: record actor_id (opaque internal id), actor_type (human|service|integration), actor_resolution_hint (string with one-line human name and principal email if available), and saml_link_id to reference the SSO assertion linkage. Do not persist raw SAML assertion; keep a short assertion id and identity provider alias for traceability.

Impersonation and delegation: capture fields 'effective_actor_id' and 'auth_path' as a comma-separated list when impersonation occurs (e.g., 'user:U123,token:svc-9,admin-as-user:U900'). These remain strings in the envelope.

RBAC v2 specifics: when a role assignment or policy is edited, prefer emitting a single event with both MOP diffs and pre/post digests. Additionally emit granular sub-events for 'privilege_escalation' when a change increases a principal's effective privileges above a configured risk threshold.

Redaction rules: PII fields should be redacted at source using a standard pattern 'REDACTED:<reason>'. Examples: replace password/hash values, raw certificate PEMs. SAML assertion bodies are never stored, only assertion id and idp_alias.

Integrity and non-repudiation: include a signature_hint field with the key id used to HMAC the base envelope for high-sensitivity events. Full signature verification is offloaded to an archival verification job.

Indexing strategy: index event_id, ts, event_type, actor_id, target_id, request_id, trace_id, saml_link_id, outcome, and severity. Store diff_blob in object storage tier with a pointer (diff_blob_ref) if blob sizes are large.

Retention classes: short_term (90d) for low-sensitivity operational events, medium_term (1yr) for admin actions, legal_hold_required (indefinite) for events tied to customer audits or security incidents. Mapping rules documented and plumbed into the pipeline.

Consumer contract: Console, SIEM exporter, and internal incident workflows can request either 'envelope-only' (metadata) or 'full-reconstruction' (apply MOP to resolved pre-state stored in state service). Provide libraries that apply MOP into a JSON snapshot for downstream use.

Migration guidance: existing audit producers should map their 'action' to the canonical event_type vocabulary and emit an 'intent' string. A transition shim will accept legacy events and populate minimal fields for 12 months after rollout.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Chose MOP over JSON Patch because common admin edits are semantically small and MOP lines compress better and are more readable in alerts. Tradeoff: requires a small parser library that consumers must adopt.

Store digests instead of full pre/post snapshots to save storage and reduce accidental PII retention. Tradeoff: cannot reconstruct state from digest alone; reconstruction must query the authoritative state service when needed.

Avoid persisting raw SAML assertions for privacy and size; instead keep assertion ids and idp aliases. Tradeoff: deep forensics that require the original assertion will need operator cooperation (IdP logs).
Retain full_snapshot for complex edits or legal_hold events despite higher cost to satisfy compliance requests.
open_blockers_and_risks: Finalize canonical vocabulary for intent and event_type (security/PM alignment required).
Security review pending on redaction patterns for nested sensitive fields (Priya Nair assigned).
Need decision on default size threshold for switching from MOP to full_snapshot (proposal: 16KB) and S3 vs internal blobstore for large diffs.
Consumer migration risk: Console and SIEM teams must adopt MOP decoder. Provide a compatibility library in two languages (Go, Python) before rollout.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Finalize schema document and vocabulary; secure SecEng review and privacy sign-off.
Week 2: Implement server-side MOP encoder, pre/post digest calculator, and redaction hooks in authz service; land library in internal monorepo.
Week 3: Provide consumer libraries (Go/Python), update Console ingestion and SIEM exporter to decode MOP for display and alerts.
Week 4: Run compatibility shim for legacy events, start small canary with internal customers, observe storage/ingestion metrics and iterate.
Post-release: Add archival verification job that checks signature_hint HMACs nightly for high-severity events.
